title: Functorial embedding of a tower into a split tower with split cokernel
statement: Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian]. Call an inverse system $(X_n,g_n:X_{n+1}\to X_n)_{n\geq1}$ in $\mathcal A$ [def-weil-inverse-system] *split* if every $g_n$ has a right inverse, i.e. there are $\sigma_n:X_n\to X_{n+1}$ with $g_n\circ\sigma_n=\mathrm{id}_{X_n}$. For an inverse system $T=(T_n,f_n)$ write $f_{m,n}=f_n\circ f_{n+1}\circ\cdots\circ f_{m-1}:T_m\to T_n$ for $m\geq n$ ($f_{n,n}=\mathrm{id}$), and let $E(T)$ be the inverse system with $E(T)_m=\prod_{n=1}^mT_n$ (a finite product) and transition maps $E(T)_{m+1}\to E(T)_m$ the projections forgetting the factor $T_{m+1}$; for a morphism $\varphi=(\varphi_n):T\to T'$ let $E(\varphi)_m=\prod_{n\le m}\varphi_n$. Let $j_T:T\to E(T)$ have components $j_{T,m}=(f_{m,n})_{n\le m}:T_m\to\prod_{n\le m}T_n$. Then $E$ is an additive functor from inverse systems in $\mathcal A$ to inverse systems in $\mathcal A$ (i.e. a functor with $E(\varphi+\psi)=E(\varphi)+E(\psi)$, morphisms of inverse systems being added levelwise), $j_T$ is a morphism of inverse systems natural in $T$ (i.e. $E(\varphi)\circ j_T=j_{T'}\circ\varphi$), every $j_{T,m}$ is a monomorphism, and both $E(T)$ and the levelwise cokernel $C(T)=(\operatorname{coker}j_{T,m})_m$, with its induced transition maps, are split inverse systems.

proof.text: Notation. By [def-sp-abelian] $\mathcal A$ has finite biproducts. For $m\ge1$ fix the biproduct $E(T)_m=\prod_{n=1}^mT_n$ with projections $\mathrm{pr}_n$ and injections $\mathrm{in}_n$, satisfying $\mathrm{pr}_n\mathrm{in}_n=\mathrm{id}$, $\mathrm{pr}_k\mathrm{in}_n=0$ for $k\neq n$ and $\sum_{n\le m}\mathrm{in}_n\mathrm{pr}_n=\mathrm{id}$ (the identities of [def-weil-additive-category], iterated); for $m=1$ it is $T_1$, and the empty product $\prod_{n<1}T_n$ is the zero object. A morphism $Y\to\prod_{n\le m}T_n$ is determined by its components $\mathrm{pr}_n\circ(-)$, and composition is bilinear [def-weil-preadditive-category]. We identify $\prod_{n\le m+1}T_n=\big(\prod_{n\le m}T_n\big)\oplus T_{m+1}$; the transition map $e_m:E(T)_{m+1}\to E(T)_m$ is the morphism with $\mathrm{pr}_ne_m=\mathrm{pr}_n$ for $n\le m$. From the definition of $f_{m,n}$ [def-weil-inverse-system]: $f_{m+1,n}=f_{m,n}\circ f_m$ for $n\le m$, and $f_{m,m}=\mathrm{id}$.

source.place: Lemma 070M (lemma-difficulty-K-injectives), proof: the decompositions $I_{n+1}^p=C_{n+1}^p\oplus I_n^p$ (agent-written realization)

proof.text: $E$ is an additive functor. For $\varphi:T\to T'$, $E(\varphi)_m$ is the morphism with $\mathrm{pr}_nE(\varphi)_m=\varphi_n\mathrm{pr}_n$ ($n\le m$). It is a morphism of inverse systems [def-weil-inverse-system]: for $n\le m$, $\mathrm{pr}_ne'_mE(\varphi)_{m+1}=\mathrm{pr}_nE(\varphi)_{m+1}=\varphi_n\mathrm{pr}_n=\varphi_n\mathrm{pr}_ne_m=\mathrm{pr}_nE(\varphi)_me_m$. Comparing components, $E(\mathrm{id})=\mathrm{id}$, $E(\psi\varphi)=E(\psi)E(\varphi)$ (as $\mathrm{pr}_nE(\psi)_mE(\varphi)_m=\psi_n\mathrm{pr}_nE(\varphi)_m=\psi_n\varphi_n\mathrm{pr}_n$), and, by bilinearity of composition [def-weil-preadditive-category], $\mathrm{pr}_nE(\varphi+\psi)_m=(\varphi_n+\psi_n)\mathrm{pr}_n=\mathrm{pr}_n(E(\varphi)_m+E(\psi)_m)$, so $E(\varphi+\psi)=E(\varphi)+E(\psi)$ for the levelwise sum.

source.place: Lemma 070M (lemma-difficulty-K-injectives), proof: the decompositions $I_{n+1}^p=C_{n+1}^p\oplus I_n^p$ (agent-written realization)

proof.text: $E(T)$ is split. Let $\sigma_m=\mathrm{in}^{(m+1)}_{\le m}:E(T)_m\to E(T)_{m+1}$ be the injection of the summand $\prod_{n\le m}T_n$ of $E(T)_{m+1}=\big(\prod_{n\le m}T_n\big)\oplus T_{m+1}$, i.e. $\mathrm{pr}_n\sigma_m=\mathrm{pr}_n$ for $n\le m$ and $\mathrm{pr}_{m+1}\sigma_m=0$. Then $\mathrm{pr}_ne_m\sigma_m=\mathrm{pr}_n\sigma_m=\mathrm{pr}_n$ for all $n\le m$, so $e_m\sigma_m=\mathrm{id}_{E(T)_m}$ and every transition map of $E(T)$ has a right inverse.

source.place: Lemma 070M (lemma-difficulty-K-injectives), proof: the decompositions $I_{n+1}^p=C_{n+1}^p\oplus I_n^p$ (agent-written realization)

proof.text: $j_T$ is a natural monomorphism of inverse systems. (a) Morphism of inverse systems: for $n\le m$, $\mathrm{pr}_ne_mj_{T,m+1}=\mathrm{pr}_nj_{T,m+1}=f_{m+1,n}=f_{m,n}f_m=\mathrm{pr}_nj_{T,m}f_m$ (Step 1), so $e_mj_{T,m+1}=j_{T,m}f_m$. (b) Naturality: for $\varphi:T\to T'$ and $n\le m$, iterating $f'_k\varphi_{k+1}=\varphi_kf_k$ ($k=n,\dots,m-1$) gives $f'_{m,n}\varphi_m=\varphi_nf_{m,n}$, hence $\mathrm{pr}_nE(\varphi)_mj_{T,m}=\varphi_nf_{m,n}=f'_{m,n}\varphi_m=\mathrm{pr}_nj_{T',m}\varphi_m$, i.e. $E(\varphi)\circ j_T=j_{T'}\circ\varphi$. (c) Mono: $\mathrm{pr}_mj_{T,m}=f_{m,m}=\mathrm{id}_{T_m}$, so $j_{T,m}$ has a left inverse and is a monomorphism ($j_{T,m}a=j_{T,m}b\Rightarrow a=\mathrm{pr}_mj_{T,m}a=\mathrm{pr}_mj_{T,m}b=b$). By [lem-weil-tower-category-levelwise-abelian], $j_T$ is then a monomorphism of $\operatorname{Tow}(\mathcal A)$ and its cokernel there is the levelwise cokernel $C(T)$ with the induced transition maps.

source.place: Lemma 070M (lemma-difficulty-K-injectives), proof: the decompositions $I_{n+1}^p=C_{n+1}^p\oplus I_n^p$ (agent-written realization)

proof.text: The cokernel at level $m$. Let $\theta_m:E(T)_m\to E(T)_m$ be given by $\mathrm{pr}_n\theta_m=\mathrm{pr}_n-f_{m,n}\mathrm{pr}_m$ for $n<m$ and $\mathrm{pr}_m\theta_m=\mathrm{pr}_m$ (in elements: $(t_n)_{n\le m}\mapsto((t_n-f_{m,n}t_m)_{n<m},t_m)$). It is an automorphism, with inverse $\theta'_m$ given by $\mathrm{pr}_n\theta'_m=\mathrm{pr}_n+f_{m,n}\mathrm{pr}_m$ ($n<m$), $\mathrm{pr}_m\theta'_m=\mathrm{pr}_m$: componentwise, $\mathrm{pr}_n\theta_m\theta'_m=\mathrm{pr}_n+f_{m,n}\mathrm{pr}_m-f_{m,n}\mathrm{pr}_m=\mathrm{pr}_n$, and likewise for $\theta'_m\theta_m$. Moreover $\mathrm{pr}_n\theta_mj_{T,m}=f_{m,n}-f_{m,n}f_{m,m}=0$ for $n<m$ and $\mathrm{pr}_m\theta_mj_{T,m}=\mathrm{id}$, so $\theta_mj_{T,m}=\mathrm{in}_m$, the injection of the summand $T_m$ in $E(T)_m=T_m\oplus\prod_{n<m}T_n$. In a biproduct $A\oplus B$ the projection $p_B$ is a cokernel of $i_A$ [def-weil-additive-category]: $p_Bi_A=0$, and if $gi_A=0$ then $g=g(i_Ap_A+i_Bp_B)=(gi_B)p_B$, uniquely since $p_Bi_B=\mathrm{id}$ makes $p_B$ an epimorphism. Transporting along $\theta_m$: $\pi_m:=p_{<m}\theta_m:E(T)_m\to\prod_{n<m}T_n$, i.e. $\mathrm{pr}_n\pi_m=\mathrm{pr}_n-f_{m,n}\mathrm{pr}_m$ ($n<m$), is a cokernel of $j_{T,m}=\theta_m^{-1}\mathrm{in}_m$ (a morphism $g$ kills $j_{T,m}$ iff $g\theta_m^{-1}$ kills $\mathrm{in}_m$). So $0\to T_m\xrightarrow{j_{T,m}}E(T)_m\xrightarrow{\pi_m}\prod_{n<m}T_n\to0$ is split exact and we may take $C(T)_m=\prod_{n<m}T_n$ ($C(T)_1=0$). This is the source's $I_{n+1}^p=C_{n+1}^p\oplus I_n^p$ in this situation: $E(T)_m=j_{T,m}(T_m)\oplus\theta_m^{-1}(\prod_{n<m}T_n)$.

source.place: Lemma 070M (lemma-difficulty-K-injectives), proof: the decompositions $I_{n+1}^p=C_{n+1}^p\oplus I_n^p$ (agent-written realization)

proof.text: $C(T)$ is split. The induced transition map $c_m:C(T)_{m+1}=\prod_{n\le m}T_n\to C(T)_m=\prod_{n<m}T_n$ is the unique morphism with $c_m\pi_{m+1}=\pi_me_m$ (it exists by Step 5, as $\pi_me_mj_{T,m+1}=\pi_mj_{T,m}f_m=0$ by Step 4(a)). We claim $c_m=\pi_m$ (on $\prod_{n\le m}T_n=E(T)_m$). Indeed, for $n<m$, using $f_{m+1,n}=f_{m,n}f_m$ and $f_{m+1,m}=f_m$: $\mathrm{pr}_n\pi_m\pi_{m+1}=\mathrm{pr}_n\pi_{m+1}-f_{m,n}\mathrm{pr}_m\pi_{m+1}=(\mathrm{pr}_n-f_{m+1,n}\mathrm{pr}_{m+1})-f_{m,n}(\mathrm{pr}_m-f_m\mathrm{pr}_{m+1})=\mathrm{pr}_n-f_{m,n}\mathrm{pr}_m=\mathrm{pr}_n\pi_me_m$ (the last as $\mathrm{pr}_ke_m=\mathrm{pr}_k$ for $k\le m$), so $\pi_m\pi_{m+1}=\pi_me_m$ and $c_m=\pi_m$ by uniqueness. Let $\kappa_m:\prod_{n<m}T_n\to\prod_{n\le m}T_n$ be the injection of the summand ($\mathrm{pr}_n\kappa_m=\mathrm{pr}_n$ for $n<m$, $\mathrm{pr}_m\kappa_m=0$); then $\mathrm{pr}_n\pi_m\kappa_m=\mathrm{pr}_n-f_{m,n}\cdot0=\mathrm{pr}_n$, so $c_m\kappa_m=\mathrm{id}$. Any other choice of the cokernels $\operatorname{coker}j_{T,m}$ is isomorphic to this one by isomorphisms compatible with the induced transition maps (uniqueness of cokernels and of the induced maps), and conjugating $\kappa_m$ by these isomorphisms gives right inverses there. Hence $C(T)$ is a split inverse system, which completes the proof.
